name: WhisperWolf
description: WhisperWolf: A Monte Carlo Benchmark for Small LLMs in a Social Deduction Game Multi‑agent conversational games such as Werewolf offer a valuable testbed for evaluating the social reasoning, deception and persuasion abilities of large language models. This work presents WhisperWolf, a reproducible Monte‑Carlo benchmark built for locally‑runnable small‑scale LLMs (2.7B‑7B parameters). We design a modular five‑layer prompt architecture which decouples agent role and personality, and implement both public discussion and private “whisper” secret communication channels to simulate information asymmetry in multi‑agent environments. We conduct 450 automated Werewolf‑game experiments across five open‑source small LLMs to answer three research questions: how model size and architecture affect strategic performance; how personality‑oriented prompting shapes agent behaviour; and how private communication influences multi‑agent dynamics. Experimental results show that within 2.7B‑7B parameter range, model parameter count alone cannot determine game performance. LLaMA 3.2 3B achieves the highest overall win rate, outperforming larger 7B‑parameter models. Concise response style and low role‑information leakage are strongly correlated with better strategic performance. Besides, agent personality settings and private whisper channels bring significant impacts on faction win rates. All code, prompts and experimental data are open‑sourced.
